MEETING DATE: July14, 2004

SUBJECT: Procurement Authorization - Supply Of Currency Packaging For A Three-Year Contract
Term




RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Commission approve the issuance of Purchase Orders to the following
companies for the supply of currency packaging for a three-year period from September 1, 2004 to August
31, 2007:

1. Grand and Toy in the upset limit amount of $240,000, and

2. Corporate Express Canada, Inc. in the upset limit of $185,000.


FUNDING

Sufficient funds are included in the 2004 TTC Operating Budget and funding will be included in future
Operating Budgets as required.


BACKGROUND

The Commission has a daily need of twenty-two currency packaging items, such as coin wrappers,
corrugated coin cartons, plastic and canvas bags, etc. These items must be available to Revenue Operations
on a long-term direct supply contract in which the supplier delivers directly to the appropriate staff. The
present contract is due to expire on August 31, 2004.


DISCUSSION

Eight companies were invited to submit proposals in addition to the public advertisement on the TTC
website on May 6, 2004 out of which two companies submitted proposals as detailed on the attached
Appendix ‘A’.

The Request for Proposal (RFP) requested pricing for 22 items and proponents were required to provide
their current (catalogue) prices for the first year of the contract and to identify any percentage discount (firm
for the duration of the contract) that may be applicable to each item. The 22 items make up 100% of
anticipated expenditures and the quantities used for pricing each item are based on actual historical usage
over a 12 month period. The RFP provided for the option of awarding the complete shopping basket to one
company or awarding each item to the proponent with the lowest price per item.

Prices for year 2 and 3 are subject to adjustment on a quarterly basis commencing on September 1, 2005
based on changes to the Industrial Price Index.

The RFP included an option for an additional two years to the contract (i.e. years 4 and 5) to be exercised at
the TTC’s discretion on the basis of the same terms and conditions and subject to satisfactory performance
by the company.

Grand & Toy Ltd. (Grand & Toy) submitted the lower overall proposal pricing for 21 of the shopping
basket items. They did not quote on one item (canvas bags) as they are unable to supply this item. Grand &
Toy did not state any exceptions or qualifications and are considered commercially compliant.
 Corporate Express Canada Inc. submitted the second proposal and quoted on all the 22 items of the
shopping basket. They did not state any exceptions or qualifications and their proposal is considered
commercially compliant.

Staff performed an analysis of the savings if the contract was awarded to the lower proponent per line item
versus the lower overall proponent. This analysis revealed a savings of approximately $10,000 per year if
each item was awarded to the lower bidder. Therefore,
staff recommends the award of 14 items in the upset limit of $240,000 to Grand & Toy and the award of 8
items in the upset limit of $185,000 to Corporate Express.

A price comparison over the current contract with Corporate Express revealed an overall decrease of
approximately 9% over the proposed pricing for year 1. The prices for year 2 and 3 are subject to
adjustment per changes in the IPI for Toronto.

The upset limit amounts for both companies include an allowance of approximately 20% to allow for
variation in actual usage and for price escalation over the three years of the contract.

The contract is recommend for award for a three-year period and prior to the contracts expiry staff will
review the companies’ performance and will determine the pricing for years 4 and 5 based on changes to
IPI. A decision regarding the extension for the 4th and 5th year will be based on the performance of the
companies and will be the subject of a future report.

Some of the reasons that the other invited proponents did not bid are as follows; one company indicated
that their “retail program” was still quite new and they did not feel that they would be able to fulfil the
requirements, one company indicated that they did not bid on this requirement because their legal
department had some issues with some of the terms and conditions in the RFP, another company
indicated the requirement was not part of their core business and they would have had to source some of
the items, and bring them into stock just for the Commission, therefore they decided not to bid and one
company indicated that the manufacturer of the coin wrappers would not sell to them.




JUSTIFICATION

Approval of this report will ensure the uninterrupted supply of currency packaging materials for the
Commission’s ongoing business requirements.

               ACTION ITEM:                     X




               RECOMMENDATION

               It is recommended that the Commission authorize the award of three-year inventory supply
               contracts for the supply of various electronic parts to the following companies for the period
               from November 2008 to November 2011:

                           -   CEA Telecom Incorporated for $680,000 including applicable taxes.

                           -   Newark for $558,000 including applicable taxes.

                           -   Electro Sonic Incorporated for $395,000 including applicable taxes.

                           -   Wesco Distribution Canada LP for $192,000 including applicable taxes.

                           -   Richardson Electronics Canada Limited for $45,000 including applicable taxes.

                           -   Anixter Canada Incorporated for $13,000 including applicable taxes.


               FUNDING

               Sufficient funds are available in the 2008 TTC Operating Budget and will be included in
               future Operating Budgets as appropriate. These inventory materials will be charged to the
               appropriate budget at the time of issuance from Stores.


               BACKGROUND

               The subject electronic parts are used for varying maintenance needs throughout the
               Commission.
 PROCUREMENT AUTHORIZATION - SUPPLY OF
VARIOUS ELECTRONIC PARTS                                                                  Page 2



DISCUSSION

Proposals were invited from twenty-seven known companies coupled with an advertisement
on the TTC internet website on July 28, 2008. Seven companies submitted proposals as
summarized in Appendix ‘A’.

The proposal called for 693 pre-approved part types. The proponents were also advised that
alternatives would not be considered during the evaluation. A total of 586 part types are
being recommended for award. The 107 part types that are not being recommended for
award are comprised of 105 part types where no pricing was received, 1 part type that was
deselected due to excessive price increases and 1 part type that was deselected as the only
proponent to offer pricing did not include the required delivery lead time. Staff will investigate
these parts and they may subsequently be the subject of a future tender.

CEA Telecom Incorporated submitted prices on 167 part types and has the lowest price on
59 part types. Of the 59 part types, 1 was deselected as the pricing received was
approximately 2,700% higher than current pricing. There were no other prices received for
this part type. Staff deemed this as an obvious error. As well, they were tied as the low
bidder with two other companies for 1 additional part type, however the other two
companies offered better delivery lead times, therefore CEA Telecom Incorporated are
recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract of $680,000 for 58 part types.

Newark submitted prices on 435 part types and has the lowest price on 358 part types. As
well, they were tied as the low bidder with Richardson Electronics Canada Limited for 1
additional part type. Though Newark offered the same delivery lead time as Richardson
Electronics Canada Limited (Richardson), their on-time delivery performance rating was not as
good as Richardson’s, therefore the part is being recommended for award to Richardson. Of
the 358 part types, 1 was deselected from their evaluation as the only pricing received was
99% lower when compared to the next low bid and current pricing. Staff have deemed this
as an obvious error and recommend this part type to be awarded to the next lowest
proponent – Electro Sonic Incorporated. Their offer also included qualifications regarding
minimum orders and packaging for 44 part types within the 358. These were reviewed by
staff and deemed as acceptable. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit
contract of $558,000 for 358 part types.

Electro Sonic Incorporated submitted prices on 376 part types and has the lowest price on
127 part types, inclusive of the 1 part type deselected from Newark. Their proposal also
contained pricing for 1 other part type, however they did not provide the required delivery
lead time for that part type thereby rendering it as non-compliant and was not considered
further. As no other prices were received for this part type, it was no longer considered in
the evaluation. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract of $395,000
for 127 part types.
 PROCUREMENT AUTHORIZATION - SUPPLY OF
VARIOUS ELECTRONIC PARTS                                                              Page 3



Wesco Distribution Canada LP submitted prices on 39 part types and has the lowest price on
24 part types. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract of $192,000
for 24 part types.

Richardson Electronics Canada Limited submitted prices on 74 part types and has the lowest
price on 9 part types inclusive of the 1 part type deselected from Newark. They are
recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract of $45,000 for 9 part types.

Anixter Canada Incorporated submitted prices on 159 part types and has the lowest price on
11 part types. Their proposal also contained pricing for 1 other part type, however that part
type was deemed as an alternative thereby rendering it as non-compliant and was not
considered further. Their offer also included qualifications regarding minimum orders and
packaging for 2 part types within the 11. These were reviewed by staff and only 1 part type
is deemed as acceptable. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract of
$13,000 for 10 part types.

Intrepid Distributors submitted prices on 362 part types, however they did not provide the
required delivery lead times in the proposal thereby rendering their proposal as non-compliant
and was not considered further.

Each contract includes approximately 20% contingency for variances between forecasted
and actual usage and new parts yet to be identified which may be added to the contracts
during the contract term.

The pricing for the new three-year inventory supply contracts are approximately 11% lower
in the first year of the contract based on current pricing. The pricing will be approximately
4% higher in year two based on year one pricing and approximately 5% higher in year three
based on year two pricing.


JUSTIFICATION

These electronic parts are required in order to support varying electronic maintenance needs
throughout the Commission.

SUBJECT: Procurement Authorization – Purchase of Bus Brake Drums




RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Commission authorize the award of three-year inventory supply contracts for the
supply of various bus brake drums to the following companies for the period from March 2007 to March
2010:

-       Bartlett-Provincial Brake Inc. for $953,000 including applicable taxes.

-       Harper Freightliner Inc. for $482,000 including applicable taxes.


FUNDING

Sufficient funds have been included in the 2007 TTC Operating Budget and will be included in future
Operating Budgets as appropriate. These inventory items will be charged to the appropriate budget at the
time of issuance from Stores.


BACKGROUND

The subject bus brake drums are used to maintain the braking systems on the Commission’s buses.


DISCUSSION

Proposals were invited from fifteen known companies coupled with an advertisement on the TTC internet
website on November 20, 2006. Twelve companies submitted proposals as summarized in Appendix ‘A’.

The proposal called for 5 pre-approved part types. The proponents were also advised that alternatives would
not be considered during the evaluation. All 5 parts types are being recommended for award.

Bartlett-Provincial Brake Inc. submitted pricing on 5 part types and has the lowest compliant price on 4 part
types. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $953,000 for the 4 part types.
Harper Freightliner Inc. submitted pricing on 5 part types and has the lowest compliant price on 1 part type.
They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $482,000 for the 1 part type.

Truck Trailer Transit Inc. submitted pricing on 5 part types. Their submission is quoted in US dollars. Staff
converted their pricing based on the published rate of 1.1474, however they did not offer the lowest price on
any of the part types. They are not being recommended for award of any part types.

New Flyer Industries Limited submitted pricing on 1 part type but was not the lowest price on the part type.
 They are not being recommended for award of the part type.

Neudoerffer Truck Supply Inc. submitted pricing on 4 part types but was not the lowest price on any of the
part types. They are not being recommended for award of any part types.

The following companies submitted pricing on 5 part types but were not the lowest price on any of the part
types and are not being recommended for award of any part types:

-       Baker Transit Parts Inc.
-       MCI Service Parts Company
-       Traction Division of UAP
-       Thorncrest Sherway Inc.
-       Daimler Chrysler Comm. Buses North America
-       Western Toronto International Trucks Inc.
-       Fort Garry Industries

The pricing for the new three-year inventory supply contracts are approximately 5% lower than current
pricing in the first year of the contract. The pricing will be approximately 1% higher in year two based on
year one pricing and no increase in year three based on year two pricing.

Each contract includes approximately 20% contingency for variances between forecasted and actual usage
and new parts yet to be identified which may be added to the contracts during the contract term.




JUSTIFICATION

These brake drums are required in order to support bus vehicle braking maintenance needs.

               supply of various Delco parts to the following companies for the period from June 2006 to June 2009:

               -               Elreg Distributors Limited for $384,000 including applicable taxes.

               -               Fort Garry Industries Limited for $260,000 including applicable taxes.

               -               British Auto Supply for $155,500 including applicable taxes.

               -               MCI Service Parts Incorporated for $37,500 including applicable taxes.

               -               Davies Auto Electric Limited for $7,500 including applicable taxes.

               -               Vaughan Automotive Supplies for $1,000 including applicable taxes


               FUNDING

               Sufficient funds to cover these items have been included in the 2006 TTC Operating Budget and will be
               included in future budgets as required. These inventory materials will be charged to the appropriate budget
               at the time of issuance from Stores.


               BACKGROUND
 The subject Delco parts are used primarily to maintain the electrical systems on the Commission’s
revenue and non-revenue vehicles. Several examples include spark plugs, spark plug wires, starter
solenoids and alternator drive gears.


DISCUSSION

Proposals were invited from twelve known companies coupled with an advertisement on the TTC internet
website on January 24, 2006. Eight companies submitted proposals as summarized in Appendix ‘A’.
The proposal called for 80 pre-approved part types. The proponents were also advised that alternatives
would not be considered during the evaluation. A total of 74 part types are being recommended for award.
The 6 part types that are not being recommended for award are comprised of 4 part types where no pricing
was received. Staff will investigate these parts and will try other sources of supply for these items. There is 1
part type that will be rebuilt within the Commission. As well staff has recently identified 1 part type as no
longer being required.

Elreg Distributors Limited submitted prices on 37 part types and has the lowest price on 26 part types. Their
proposal contained an exception for 6 of the 26 part types whereby there are part number changes. The
changes are deemed as administrative only with no impact to fit, form or function. Therefore, they are
recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $384,000 for 26 part types.

Fort Garry Industries Limited submitted prices on 37 part types and has the lowest price on 5 part types.
They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $260,000 for 5 part types.

British Auto Supply submitted prices on 65 part types and has the lowest price on 23 part types. Their
proposal contained an exception for 4 of the 23 part types whereby there are part number changes. The
changes are deemed as administrative only with no impact to fit, form or function. Further, staff has
deselected 2 part types as 1 will be reassigned to another grouping of parts that are categorized as being
rebuilt within the Commission and 1 has been identified as being no longer required. Therefore, they are
recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $155,500 for 21 part types.

MCI Service Parts Company submitted prices on 26 part types and has the lowest price on 7 part types.
They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $37,500 for 7 part types.

Davies Auto Electric Limited submitted prices on 58 part types and has the lowest price on 7 part types.
They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $7,500 for 7 part types.

Vaughan Automotive Supplies submitted prices on 61 part types and has the lowest price on 8 part types.
They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $1,000 for 8 part types.

Avenue Motor Works submitted prices on 57 part types however they did not acknowledge the TTC issued
addendum as required thereby rendering their proposal as non-compliant and they were not considered
further.

General Auto Parts submitted prices on 62 part types, however their proposal was incomplete as it did not
contain the required lead times rendering their proposal as non-compliant and was not considered further.

Each contract includes approximately 20% contingency for variances between forecasted and actual usage
and new parts yet to be identified which may be added to the contracts during the contract term.

The pricing for the new three-year inventory supply contracts are approximately 2% lower in the first year
 of the contract. The pricing will be approximately 4% higher in year two based on year one pricing and
approximately 4% higher in year three based on year two pricing.


JUSTIFICATION

These Delco parts are required in order to maintain the electrical systems on the Commission’s revenue
and non-revenue vehicles.

SUBJECT: Purchase Of Filters




RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Commission authorize the award of three-year inventory supply contracts for the
supply of various filters to the following companies for the period from May 2006 to May 2009:

-           Freightliner Mid-Ontario Incorporated for $47,000 including applicable taxes.

FUNDING

Sufficient funds to cover these items have been included in the 2006 TTC Operating Budget and will be
included in future budgets as required. These inventory materials will be charged to the appropriate budget
at the time of issuance from Stores.


BACKGROUND

The subject filters are used for varying filtering needs throughout the Commission’s vehicles and
properties. Several examples include spray booth filters, fuel filters, oil filters, vehicle air filters and
transmission oil filters.




DISCUSSION

Proposals were invited from seventeen known companies coupled with an advertisement on the TTC
internet website on January 25, 2006. Twelve companies submitted proposals as summarized in Appendix
‘A’.

The proposal called for 74 pre-approved part types. The proponents were also advised that alternatives
would not be considered during the evaluation. A total of 59 part types are being recommended for award.
The 15 part types that are not being recommended for award are comprised of 14 part types where no
 pricing was received. Staff will investigate these parts and will try other sources of supply for these items.
There is 1 part type where pricing was deemed as excessive. Staff will review this part and it may be the
subject of a future proposal.

Harper Detroit Diesel submitted prices on 29 part types and has the lowest price on 20 part types. They are
recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $366,000 for 20 part types.

Cummins Eastern Canada LP submitted prices on 10 part types and has the lowest price on 1 part type.

recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $71,000 for 4 part types.

are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $47,000 for 5 part types.

recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $1,000 for 1 part type.

Allmake Select Auto Parts Incorporated submitted prices on 31 part types, however their proposal was

Each contract includes approximately 20% contingency for variances between forecasted and actual usage
and new parts yet to be identified which may be added to the contracts during the contract term.
 The pricing for the new three-year inventory supply contracts are approximately 19% lower in the first year
of the contract. The pricing will be approximately 4% higher in year two based on year one pricing and
approximately 4% higher in year three based on year two pricing.


JUSTIFICATION

These filters are required for varying filtering needs throughout the Commission’s vehicles and properties.

has estimated that over the three year period, these 4 part types will be required to support

                                  TORONTO TRANSIT COMMISSION
                                          REPORT NO.

               SUBJECT:                    PROCUREMENT AUTHORIZATION – SUPPLY OF OFFICE
                                           SUPPLIES, TONER AND COPIER PAPER FOR A 5 YEAR
                                           PERIOD.

               ACTION ITEM:


               RECOMMENDATION

               It is recommended that the Commission approve the issuance of a purchase order in the total
               upset limit of $9,000,000 to Staples Advantage for the supply of office supplies, toner and
               copier paper for a 5 year period from August 1, 2009 to July 31, 2014.

               FUNDING

               Sufficient funds are included in the 2009 TTC Operating Budget and will be included in future
               Operating Budgets as required.


               BACKGROUND

               At its meeting of July 14, 2004 the Commission approved the award of a contract to
               Corporate Express Canada Ltd. (CEC) in the upset amount of $4,100,000 for the supply of
               office supplies, toner and copier paper for a 3 year period from August 1, 2004 to July 31,
               2007 with the option for additional 4th and 5th year extensions, to be exercised at the
               Commission’s sole discretion. They were awarded the contract on the basis of lowest overall
               compliant proposal received.
               At its meeting of May 7, 2007 the Commission approved the issuance of a purchase order
               amendment to Corporate Express Canada Ltd. to exercise the option to extend the contract
               with Corporate Express for the two year extension to July 31, 2009 and increase the total
               upset limit amount by $3,575,000 to $7,675,000.

               On May 25, 2009 the purchase order was amended to increase the total upset limit by
               $500,000 to a revised total of $8,175,000 to cover higher than anticipated expenditures by
               TTC employees for the supply of office supplies, toner supplies and copier paper.

               DISCUSSION

               Eleven companies were invited to submit Proposals in addition to the public advertisement on
               the TTC website on February 6, 2009 out of which eight companies submitted Proposals as
               summarized in Appendix ‘A’.
 PROCUREMENT AUTHORIZATION – SUPPLY OF
OFFICE SUPPLIES, TONER AND COPIER PAPER FOR A
5 YEAR PERIOD                                                                         Page 2


A Request for Proposal (RFP) was issued requesting the services of a company/companies to
provide office products, which include office supplies (i.e. pens, binders, etc.); toner (for
printers and fax machines) and copier paper for desktop delivery on an "as required" basis to
approximately 120 separate TTC delivery locations at approximately 60 different addresses
within the City of Toronto for a 5 year period with an option to renew for an additional 2
year extension at the Commission’s sole discretion, subject to the company’s satisfactory
performance and negotiation of acceptable pricing.

The RFP indicated that currently 17% of the TTC’s office supplies are considered to be eco-
friendly; 38% of toner cartridges are remanufactured and 11% of the copier paper purchased
contains post consumer content. The RFP also indicated that upon award of the contract the
successful Proponent(s) is to work with the Commission on “Green” alternative products.
Staff will focus on and source commercially available, certified, environmentally preferable
products with the objective to replace an additional approximately 20% of the office
supplies, toner and copier paper items listed in the price schedules within a 12 month
period of award of the contract with eco-friendly products.

Proponents were required to submit pricing and discounts in accordance with the items listed
in the price schedules for each of these groups (i.e. office supplies, toner, copier paper)
based on the estimated quantities indicated (the items listed in each of these Price Schedules
are considered “Shopping Basket items”). Overall Shopping Basket items represent
approximately 87% of the Commission’s anticipated expenditures.

Proponents were also requested to provide percentage discounts, to be used for any items
not included in the Shopping Baskets for each group. These items are considered “Off-
Shopping Basket Items” and they represent approximately 13% of anticipated expenditures.

The RFP indicated that Proponents may bid on one, or any combination of the three groups
and the Commission reserve the right to make a separate award of each group, a
combination of groups, or award of all groups to one company, whichever is deemed in the
best interest of the Commission.

Proponents were requested to submit pricing on a minimum number of items in each
shopping basket of items for three groups in order to be considered qualified as follows:
Proponents were required to quote on 95% of the items for office supplies (781 of the 822
items); 95% of the items for toner (142 of the 149 items); and 90% of the items for copier
paper (71 of the 78 items), however item numbers 1-7 were mandatory.

The pricing for office supplies was required to be firm for 5 years and the pricing for toner
was to be firm for 1 year. For toner products, proponents were to provide the Manufacturer’s
Suggested Retail Price (MRSP) and the percentage discount applicable to each item. The RFP
also indicated that any proposed price increase/decrease must be substantiated in writing by
the Manufacturer, a minimum of 30 days in advance of any such proposed
increase/decrease.
 PROCUREMENT AUTHORIZATION – SUPPLY OF
OFFICE SUPPLIES, TONER AND COPIER PAPER FOR A
5 YEAR PERIOD                                                                         Page 3


The pricing for copier paper was required to be firm for 6 months. Proponents were to
provide the Current Catalogue Price and the percentage discount applicable to each item.
The RFP also indicated that any proposed price increase/decrease must be substantiated in
writing by the paper manufacturer a minimum of 30 days in advance of any such proposed
increase/decrease. The RFP also indicated that Proponents must supply paper that is Forest
Stewardship Council (FSC) certified, Ecologo or equivalent. Paper that does not meet these
specifications would not be considered.

Upon initial review of the 8 bids received, it was discovered that both Printer Solutions (PS)
and Ederick Associates Inc. (Ederick) did not submit any of the pages of the Form of Proposal
and further, Ederick did not acknowledge the addendum. As a result, both their bids were
considered non-compliant and not evaluated further.

The bids received from the remaining six proponents provided the required pricing and did not
state any exceptions or qualifications to the Commission’s General Terms and Conditions and
all are considered commercially and technically acceptable.

The following three proponents submitted the required pricing for all three groups:

Staples Advantage (Staples) (previously operating as Corporate Express Canada Ltd)
submitted the overall lowest evaluated priced proposal. They were the lowest priced proposal
for each of the 3 groups (office supplies, toner & copier paper). They did not offer any
additional rebates or incentives if awarded the total contract requirements. They have been
satisfactorily providing these services since 2004 and are recommended for award.

Grand & Toy (G&T) submitted the second overall lowest evaluated priced proposal. G&T also
offered a volume rebate if expenditures exceeded $1,000,000 per year. G&T’s proposal is
also acceptable.

Lyreco submitted the overall highest evaluated priced proposal. They did not offer any
additional rebates or incentives if awarded the total contract requirements. Lyreco’s proposal
is also acceptable.

The remaining three bidders; QRX Technology Group, ASCA Office Solutions and The
Computer Media Group submitted pricing for toner only, however none of these companies
offered toner pricing lower than that from Staples.

Staples are recommended for award of the contract in the total upset limit amount of
$9,000,000 for a five-year period from August 1, 2009 to July 31, 2014, with the option to
renew for an additional 2 years subject to satisfactory performance and acceptable pricing,
based on overall lowest evaluated proposal pricing.

The upset limit amount includes an allowance of approximately 25% to allow for any
variation in usage between forecasted and actual quantities during the contract term.
 PROCUREMENT AUTHORIZATION – SUPPLY OF
OFFICE SUPPLIES, TONER AND COPIER PAPER FOR A
5 YEAR PERIOD                                                                           Page 4


A price comparison consisting of a total of approximately 86% of all of the items in the
Shopping Baskets for the three groups, revealed an overall decrease of approximately 32% in
year one compared to current pricing. There is no increase in pricing for the Office Supplies in
years 2 to 5, inclusive. The pricing for toner is firm for one year and the price for copier
paper is firm for 6 months, thereafter, any proposed price increase/decrease for the
subsequent years must be substantiated in writing by the manufacturer within a minimum of
30 days in advance of any such proposed increase/decrease.

Staples advised that they have significantly increased their overall sales in recent years and
are able to provide lower pricing from their vendors.


JUSTIFICATION

Award of the above contract will ensure the uninterrupted supply of office supplies, toner
and copier paper for the TTC’s on going business requirements.

                TORONTO TRANSIT COMMISSION
                REPORT NO.



               MEETING DATE: MARCH 22, 2006


               SUBJECT: Purchase Of Ingersoll-Rand Parts




               RECOMMENDATION

               It is recommended that the Commission authorize the award of three-year inventory supply contracts for the
               supply of various Ingersoll-Rand parts to the following companies for the period from March 2006 to March
               2009:

               -               Ingersoll-Rand Canada Incorporated for $1,550,000 including applicable taxes.

               -               MCI Service Parts Company for $555,000 including applicable taxes.

               -               Neopart for $71,000 including applicable taxes.


               FUNDING

               Sufficient funds to cover these items have been included in the 2006 TTC Operating Budget and will be
               included in future budgets as required. These inventory materials will be charged to the appropriate budget
               at the time of issuance from Stores.


               BACKGROUND

               The subject Ingersoll-Rand parts are used for bus starter and subway car compressor maintenance needs.
               Several examples include air starter control valves, drain compressor traps and air starter cylinders.


               DISCUSSION
 Proposals were invited from thirteen known companies coupled with an advertisement on the TTC internet
website on October 13, 2005. Seven companies submitted proposals as summarized in Appendix ‘A’.

The proposal called for 112 pre-approved part types. The proponents were also advised that alternatives
would not be considered during the evaluation. A total of 98 part types are being recommended for award.
The 14 part types that are not being recommended for award are comprised of 10 part types that have been
deemed obsolete by the manufacturer. Staff will investigate these parts and based on the outcome, they may
be a part of a subsequent proposal. There are 3 part types where no pricing was received. Staff will
investigate these parts and will try other sources of supply for these items. Finally there is 1 part type
whereby staff recommend that it not be awarded to the lowest compliant proponent as the total three year
value is approximately $50 which would not warrant the issuance of a separate long term contract.

Ingersoll-Rand Canada Incorporated submitted prices on 98 part types and has the lowest price on 62 part
types. Staff identified what appeared an obvious error in pricing on 1 part type and contacted Ingersoll-Rand
Canada Incorporated who confirmed that they had indeed made an error in their pricing. In view of this
significant and obvious error, staff did not consider this item further and recommended award of this part
type to MCI Service Parts Company. Further, their proposal contained an exception regarding 20 part types.
These changes were merely administrative with no change to fit, form or function. Therefore, they are
recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $1,550,000 for 61 part types.

MCI Service Parts Company submitted prices on 36 part types and has the lowest price on 30 part types.
They are also the lowest compliant proponent on the 1 part type that was deselected from Ingersoll-Rand
Canada Inc. Therefore, they are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $555,000 for 31 part
types.

Neopart submitted prices on 37 part types and has the lowest price on 6 part types. They are recommended
to be awarded an upset limit contract for $71,000 for these 6 part types.

North American Transit Supply Company submitted prices on 37 part types and has the lowest price on 1
part type. However, the total three year value is approximately $50 which would not warrant the issuance of
a separate contract hence this part was not considered further. Staff will address the replenishment need of
this part outside of a long term contract.

Elreg Distribution Ltd. submitted prices on 34 part types and was the apparent lowest proponent on 20 part
types. They were not offering Ingersoll-Rand parts but rather alternatives therefore rendering their proposal
as non compliant and they were not considered further.

Gillig Corporation submitted prices on 36 part types. Their proposal contained an exception stating that their
warranty did not include liability to damages that may occur to Commission vehicles from any part found
defective that they supplied on this contract. Staff determined this exception to be unacceptable thereby
rendering their proposal as non compliant and they were not considered further.

New Flyer Industries Limited submitted prices on 98 part types, however they are not the lowest price on
any of those part types.
 Each contract includes approximately 20% contingency for variances between forecasted and actual usage
and new parts yet to be identified which may be added to the contracts during the contract term.

The pricing for the new three-year inventory supply contracts are approximately 4% lower in the first year
of the contract. The pricing will be approximately 1% higher in year two based on year one pricing and
approximately 1% higher in year three based on year two pricing.


JUSTIFICATION

These Ingersoll-Rand parts are required in order to support varying bus starter and subway car compressor
maintenance needs.

SUBJECT: Purchase Of Lubricating Products

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Commission authorize the award of three-year inventory
supply contracts for the supply of lubricating products to the following companies for the
period from April 2003 to March 2006:

   •   Brodi Chemicals for $370,000 including applicable taxes.

   •   British Auto Supply Company Limited for $35,000 including applicable taxes.

   •   Noco Lubricants Canada Incorporated for $24,000 including applicable taxes.

   •   Fuchs Lubricants Canada Limited for $9,000 including applicable taxes.

   •   Shell Canada Products for $6,000 including applicable taxes.

   •   Petro-Canada Lubricants for $1,000 including applicable taxes.



FUNDING

Sufficient funds have been included in the 2003 TTC Operating Budget and will be
included in future Operating Budgets as appropriate. These inventory materials will be
charged to the appropriate budget at the time of issuance from Stores.



BACKGROUND

The subject lubricants are used for various maintenance applications within the
Commission.



DISCUSSION

Proposals were invited from twenty-nine known companies coupled with an
advertisement on the TTC internet web site on January 30, 2003. Eight companies
submitted proposals as summarized in Appendix 'A'.
 The proposal called for 43 part types out of which 15 are being recommended for award.
The remaining 28 part types were a combination of 26 part types not being quoted by any
of the proponents and 2 part types with excessive price increases not considered
acceptable. Of the 26 part types that were not quoted, staff have determined the main
contributing factor as the current uncertainty in petroleum prices. The 28 part types will
be reviewed to determine a source of supply as part of a future proposal.

Brodi Chemicals has the lowest acceptable proposal on 1 part type. They are
recommended to be awarded a contract for $370,000.

British Auto Supply Company Limited has the lowest acceptable proposal on 3 part
types. They are recommended to be awarded a contract for $35,000.

Noco Lubricants Canada Incorporated has the lowest acceptable proposal on 5 part types.
They are recommended to be awarded a contract for $24,000.

Fuchs Lubricants Canada Limited has the lowest acceptable proposal on 2 part types.
They are recommended to be awarded a contract for $9,000.

Shell Canada Products has the lowest acceptable proposal on 3 part types. They are
recommended to be awarded a contract for $6,000. Their proposal contained three
qualifications. The first related to invoicing, the second was for delivery of material and
the third was for packaging of one part type. Staff has reviewed and has considered these
qualifications acceptable.

Petro-Canada Lubricants has the lowest acceptable proposal on 1 part type. They are
recommended to be awarded a contract for $1,000. Their proposal also contained pricing
on another 13 part types which were alternates. These alternates were not acceptable as
they were non-compliant to the specifications and were not considered further.

Safety-Kleen Canada Incorporated submitted a proposal on 9 part types of which all were
alternates. These alternates were not acceptable as they were non-compliant to the
specifications and were not considered further.

Vaughan Automotive Supply submitted a proposal on 4 part types however, they did not
have the lowest price on any items in the proposal.

Each contract includes approximately 20% contingency for variances between forecasted
and actual usage and new parts yet to be identified which may be added to the contracts
during the contract term.

The pricing for the new three-year inventory supply contracts are approximately 3%
higher in the first year of the contract. There will be approximately a 3% increase in year
two based on year one prices and approximately a 3% increase in year three based on
year two prices.
                JUSTIFICATION

               These lubricating products are required in order to support maintenance needs.

Subject: Procurement Authorization - Purchase Of Rockwell Meritor Brake Parts

Recommendation

It is recommended that the Commission authorize the award of three-year inventory supply
contracts for the supply of Rockwell Meritor parts to the following companies for the period from
November 2007 to November 2010:

    -   Fort Garry Industries for $1,977,000 including applicable taxes.
    -   DaimlerChrysler Commercial Buses North America Limited for $1,563,000 including
        applicable taxes.
    -   New Flyer Industries Canada ULC for $918,000 including applicable taxes.
    -   Baker Transit Parts for $85,000 including applicable taxes.
    -   Prevost Car, Incorporated for $36,000 including applicable taxes.\
    -   MCI Service Parts, Incorporated for $12,000 including applicable taxes.

Funding

Sufficient funds have been included in the 2007 TTC Operating Budget and will be included in
future Operating Budgets as appropriate. These inventory materials will be charged to the
appropriate budget at the time of issuance from Stores.

Background

The subject Rockwell Meritor parts are used for maintaining the Commission’s bus
braking system.

Discussion

Proposals were invited from twelve known companies coupled with an advertisement on the TTC
internet website on July 26, 2007. Eight companies submitted proposals as summarized in
Appendix ‘A’.

The proposal called for 220 pre-approved part types. Proponents were also advised that alternatives
would not be considered during the evaluation. A total of 211 part types are being recommended for
award. The 9 part types that are not being recommended were not priced. Staff will investigate other
sources for these parts and they may subsequently be the subject of a future proposal.

Fort Garry Industries (Fort Garry) submitted prices on 180 part types and has the lowest price on 45
part types. They were also tied with DaimlerChrysler Commercial Buses North America Limited
for the lowest price on 1 other part type, but are being recommended to be awarded this part type on
the basis of a better lead time being offered. Therefore Fort Garry is recommended to be awarded an
upset limit contract for $1,977,000 for 46 part types.
 DaimlerChrysler Commercial Buses North America Limited (Daimler) submitted prices on 205 part
types and has the lowest price on 115 part types. As well they were tied with Fort Garry on 1 part
type and New Flyer Industries Canada ULC on another part type. These two proponents offered
better lead times than Daimler and are being recommended award, therefore Daimler is
recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract of $1,563,000 for 115 part types.

New Flyer Industries Canada ULC (New Flyer) submitted prices on 184 part types and has the
lowest price on 42 part types. As well they were tied with Daimler on 1 part type. Since New Flyer
offered a better lead time than Daimler, staff have recommended award to New Flyer. Hence, they
are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $918,000 for 43 part types.

Baker Transit Parts submitted prices on 167 part types and has the lowest price on 3 part types.
They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $85,000 for 3 part types.

Prevost Car, Incorporated submitted prices on 192 part types and has the lowest price on 3 part
types. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract of $36,000 for 3 part type.

MCI Service Parts, Incorporated submitted prices on 146 part types and has the lowest price on 1
part type. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract of $12,000 for 1 part type.

Gillig Corporation submitted prices on 201 part types however they took exception to the
Commission’s warranty clause. Staff considered their exception as unacceptable therefore their
proposal was not considered further.

Western Toronto International Trucks Incorporated submitted prices on 196 part types. Their
proposal was submitted without a completed Form of Proposal as required in the proposal thereby
rendering their submission as non-compliant and was not considered further.

Each contract includes approximately 20% contingency for variances between forecasted and actual
usage and new parts yet to be identified which may be added to the contracts during the contract
term.

The pricing for the new three-year inventory supply contract is approximately 9% lower in the first
year of the contract. On this basis, staff is recommending ending the current contracts earlier than
the scheduled November 30, 2007 expiry date to take advantage of these savings. The pricing will
be approximately 2% higher in year two based on year one pricing and approximately 2% higher in
year three based on year two pricing.

Justification

These Rockwell Meritor brake parts are required in order to support bus braking maintenance
needs.

RECOMMENDATION

issuance from Stores.

examples include integrated circuits, resistors and micro-switches.

website on July 22, 2005. Eight companies submitted proposals.

The 34 part types that are not being recommended for award are comprised of 25 part types where no
pricing was received. Staff will investigate these parts and they may subsequently be the subject of a future
tender. Also, there were 7 part types which had identified excessive price increases and 2 part types that
will be re-categorized by staff.

During evaluation of the eight proposals received, three companies submitted commercially non-
compliant proposals.
 Electro-Sonic’s submission did not include required lead times, thereby rendering their proposal as
incomplete and was not considered further.

incomplete and was not considered further.

Digi-Key’s submission noted pricing that was valid to July 28, 2005, thereby rendering their proposal as
non-compliant and was not considered further.

The remaining five proposals were evaluated and will be receiving contracts as discussed below and as
summarized in Appendix ‘A’.

Newark In One submitted prices on 193 part types and has the lowest compliant price on 137 part types.
Their offer included qualifications regarding minimum orders and packaging for 34 part types within the
137. These were reviewed by staff and deemed as acceptable. Their proposal also included pricing for 17
part types that were alternatives and were not considered further for these parts. They are recommended to
be awarded an upset limit contract for $1,053,000 for these 137 part types.

CEA Telecom Incorporated submitted prices on 187 part types and has the lowest compliant price on 65
part types. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $798,000 for these 65 part
types.

Wesco Distribution Canada LP submitted prices on 28 part types and has the lowest compliant price on 19
part types. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $526,000 for these 19 part
types.

Intrepid Distributors submitted prices on 187 part types and has the lowest compliant price on 45 part types.
They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $356,000 for these 45 part types.

Richardson Electronics Canada Limited submitted prices on 15 part types and has the lowest compliant
price on 2 part types. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $11,000 for these 2
part types.
Each contract includes approximately 20% contingency for variances between forecasted and actual usage
and new parts yet to be identified which may be added to the contracts during the contract term.


The pricing for the new three-year inventory supply contracts are approximately 2% higher in the first year
of the contract based on current pricing. The pricing will be approximately 3% higher in year two based on
year one pricing and approximately 2% higher in year three based on year two pricing.


JUSTIFICATION

These electronic parts are required in order to support varying electronic maintenance needs throughout the
Commission.

SUBJECT: Purchase Of Sprague Parts

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Commission authorize the award of three-year inventory supply contracts for the
supply of Sprague parts to the following companies for the period from September 2004 to September 2007:

-           New Flyer Industries Limited for $325,000 including applicable taxes.

-           Neopart for $295,000 including applicable taxes.

-           Prevost Car Incorporated for $6,000 including applicable taxes.

-           Cadel for $3,500 including applicable taxes.


FUNDING

Sufficient funds have been included in the 2004 TTC Operating Budget and will be included in future
Operating Budgets as appropriate. These inventory materials will be charged to the appropriate budget at the
time of issuance from Stores.


BACKGROUND

The subject Sprague parts are used for maintaining the Commission’s bus, streetcar, ICTS and subway
vehicle fleet windshield wiper system. Several examples include windshield washer switches, wiper
motor piston assemblies, and left and right hand windshield wiper motor idler arms.


DISCUSSION

Tenders were invited from five known companies coupled with an advertisement on the TTC internet
website on April 30, 2004. Five companies submitted tenders as summarized in Appendix ‘A’.


The tender called for 117 pre-approved part types. Tenderers were also advised that alternatives would not
be considered during the evaluation. A total of 105 part types are being recommended for award. The 12
part types that are not being recommended were not priced. Staff will investigate these parts and they may
subsequently be the subject of a future tender.

New Flyer Industries Limited submitted prices on 99 part types and has the lowest price on 19 part types.
They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $325,000.

Neopart submitted prices on 99 part types and has the lowest price on 78 part types of which 1 part type was
tied with Cadel for the lowest price. Since Cadel has a better lead time offered, Neopart are not being
recommended award of this 1 part type. Hence, they are recommended to be awarded 77 part types for an
upset limit contract of $295,000.

Prevost Car Incorporated submitted prices on 64 part types and has the lowest price on 3 part types. They
are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $6,000.
 Cadel submitted prices on 85 part types and has the lowest price on 6 part types. They are recommended to
be awarded an upset limit contract for $3,500 for the 6 part types.

MCI Service Parts Incorporated submitted an incomplete tender and were not considered further.

Each contract includes approximately 20% contingency for variances between forecasted and actual usage
and new parts yet to be identified which may be added to the contracts during the contract term.

The pricing received for this new three-year inventory supply contract is approximately 30% higher in the
first year of the contract. The pricing will be approximately 6% higher in year two based on year one prices
and approximately 5% higher in year 3 based on year 2 prices. Staff contacted Sprague to determine the
causes for the large price increase in the first year of the contract and were advised that a new pricing
structure was implemented in September 2003. Sprague had determined following the review of their
internal costs that many of their items were costing them more to produce than what they were being sold
for.


JUSTIFICATION

These Sprague parts are required in order to support bus, streetcar, ICTS and subway vehicle windshield
wiper system maintenance needs.

SUBJECT: Procurement Authorization - Credit Card Services For The Supply Of Fuel For Non-
Revenue Vehicles

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Commission approve a contract award to Imperial Oil Limited in the total upset
limit of $3,600,000 for credit card services for the purchase of regular unleaded gasoline, diesel fuel,
propane, exterior car washes and vehicle lubrication products for non-revenue vehicles and shop equipment
over a three-year period from August 1, 2004 to July 31, 2007.


FUNDING

Sufficient funds are included in the 2004 TTC Operating Budget and will be included in future Operating
Budgets as required.


BACKGROUND

The TTC currently has a contract with Imperial Oil for credit card services for the purchase of regular
unleaded gasoline, diesel fuel, propane, exterior car washes and vehicle lubrication products at their service
stations for non-revenue vehicles and shop equipment (lawn mowers, snow throwers, lift trucks, special
saws and heaters, etc.). The current contract is scheduled to expire on July 31, 2004 and a new contract is
required for the continued supply of this service.


DISCUSSION

A Request for Proposal (RFP) was issued to five companies, in addition to a public advertisement on the
TTC web site on May 7, 2004. A total of three companies submitted proposals as summarized in Appendix
‘A’. Petro Canada submitted their bid late and it was returned to them.

Proponents were required to submit a discount per litre that would be applicable to the prevailing pump
price for unleaded gasoline (estimated usage of 1.1 million litres per year), diesel fuel (400,000 litres per
year), propane (10,000 litres per year) and the percentage discount applicable to the posted prices for the
various types of car washes available (1000 car washes per year). The quantities used for pricing were based
on actual historical usage over a 12 month period with an allowance of approximately 10% overall for
increased usage during the contract.

For evaluation purposes, staff used the average price of each fuel for the period January to June 2004, which
was escalated at a rate of 5% per year for unleaded gasoline and 4% per year for diesel and propane. The
escalation factors used are consistent with the average increases experienced over the past three years
according to information obtained from the Ontario Ministry of Energy.

Proponents were requested to provide various submission requirements to demonstrate their ability to
successfully provide the services under the contract (e.g. list of contracts of a similar size and nature,
identify the number, location and hours of operation of service stations within the City along with the list of
services provided by each e.g. diesel, car washes, propane, etc., samples of available reports, description of
security system currently in place in respect to the use of fuel credit cards, various fleet card programs
available, etc.).

Suncor Energy Products Inc. (Suncor) submitted the highest discount (4%) off the total of all monthly
purchases (includes all fuels and car washes) and did not state any exceptions or qualifications. Suncor have
 a total of 40 service stations located in the City of which 11 offer diesel, however none of their stations can
provide propane as requested. Also 22 stations are self serve, 18 are full service and 17 stations offer 24-
hour operation. Since 18 stations or 45% of their total stations are full service, which can charge up to $0.04
more per litre for fuel, the overall cost to the TTC for fuel is likely to be higher from Suncor, which may
offset some or all of the difference between Suncor and the second lowest proponent.

Suncor does not have any recent experience with a contract of a similar size to the Commission’s
requirement. In addition, Suncor’s has the least number of stations and they are not evenly distributed
throughout the City. For example, Suncor have only one service station in the “downtown” area south of St.
Clair Avenue between Coxwell Avenue in the east and Runnymede Street in the west. Further this station is
located on the border of this area (i.e. near the intersection of Runnymede Road and St. Clair) and it cannot
provide diesel fuel. Based on the number of TTC facilities in this area (e.g. substations, Roncevalles and
Russel carhouses, Hillcrest Yard and Revenue Operations, Greenwood Yard, etc.) and the number of
projects that regularly occur within this area that rely on fuel for the operation of their vehicles (e.g. track
replacement, pole and overhead traction power line replacement) Suncor does not have sufficient stations
located within a reasonable distance of the TTC’s facilities to adequately provide the required service and
further, they cannot supply propane. Therefore, Suncor’s proposal is considered non compliant and is not
recommended for award.

Imperial Oil Limited submitted the second highest discount (3.9%) off all fuel purchases, but did not offer
any discount for car washes. Imperial Oil has 82 service stations of which 25 dispense diesel and 2 stations
have propane available. Also 79 stations are self serve, 3 are full service and 54 stations offer 24-hour
operation. In comparison to Suncor, in the previously noted “downtown” area Imperial Oil has 12 service
stations of which 6 can supply diesel, which is considered acceptable.



Imperial Oil took exception to several of the Commission’s General Conditions (e.g. Indemnification,
Changes to the Work, Claims, etc.) and they also provided their own terms and conditions, which staff
determined were not applicable to the nature of the contract. In any event, staff has reviewed these
exceptions and qualifications and found them to be acceptable. Imperial Oil is the current contractor for this
service and is performing the work in a satisfactory manner. Their proposal is considered commercially and
technically acceptable and they are recommended for award.

Shell Canada Products (Shell) submitted the lowest discount of $0.0275 per litre off the price of gasoline
and diesel fuel, $0.01 per litre off the price of propane and a 25% discount off all car washes. Shell did not
state any exceptions or qualifications and has 69 service stations of which 8 dispense diesel and 2 dispense
propane. Also 62 stations are self serve, 7 are full service and 64 stations offer 24-hour operation. While
Shell has a number of service stations located throughout the City, their stations that can provide diesel are
not well distributed in the areas required by the TTC. In the previously noted “downtown” area they have a
total of 18 stations, but none of them can supply diesel. This is not considered sufficient to properly service
the TTC’s requirements since 27% of the TTC’s fuel requirements are for diesel and many diesel vehicles
have a home base at the Hillcrest Yard (e.g. Revenue Operations, Streetcar Maintenance, Electrical, etc.).
Therefore their proposal is considered unacceptable.

The current discount offered by Imperial Oil for gasoline, diesel and propane is $0.03 per litre and their
offered rate of 3.9% will result in a higher discount if the price of each of these products is above $0.76 per
litre. In June 2004 the average price for unleaded gasoline and diesel was $0.754 and $0.718, respectively,
however as fuel prices are anticipated to rise over the next 3 years, the 3.9% percentage discount off the
prevailing fuel price per litre will likely result in a higher actual discount than the current contract.

The recommended upset limit amount includes an allowance of approximately 5% for higher than
anticipated increases in the price of fuel or usage over the three-years of the contract.
 JUSTIFICATION

Award of this contract will ensure the uninterrupted supply of unleaded gasoline, diesel fuel, propane,
exterior car washes and lubrication products for the Commission’s fleet of non-revenue vehicles and shop
equipment for ongoing requirements for the next three years.

SUBJECT: Purchase Of Lift-U Parts




RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Commission authorize the award of one-year inventory supply contracts for the
supply of various Lift-U parts to the following companies for the period from May 2006 to May 2007:

-            Midwest Bus Corporation for $202,000 USD (approximately $235,000 CAD) including
applicable taxes.

-           Orion Bus Industries Limited for $147,000 CAD including applicable taxes.


FUNDING

Sufficient funds to cover these items have been included in the 2006 TTC Operating Budget and will be
included in future budgets as required. These inventory materials will be charged to the appropriate budget
at the time of issuance from Stores.


BACKGROUND

The subject Lift-U parts are used in the maintenance of wheelchair lifts on the Commission’s equipped
buses. Several examples include hydraulic hose assemblies, motor assemblies and compression springs.


DISCUSSION

Proposals were invited from ten known companies coupled with an advertisement on the TTC internet
website on March 14, 2006 for a three-year contract term. Three companies submitted proposals as
summarized in Appendix ‘A’.

The proposal called for 79 pre-approved part types. The proponents were also advised that alternatives
would not be considered during the evaluation. All 79 part types are being recommended for award.
 Midwest Bus Corporation submitted prices on all 79 part types and has the lowest price on 61 part types for
the one-year term. Their proposal was quoted in US dollars and was converted by staff using the exchange
rate of 1.1616. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $202,000 USD ($235,000
CAD) for these 61 part types.

Orion Bus Industries Limited submitted prices on 78 part types and has the lowest price on 18 part types for
the one-year term. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $147,000 CAD for
these 18 part types.

Gillig Corporation submitted prices on all 79 part types, however their proposal contained an exception to
the Commission’s one year warranty clause by offering a 6 month warranty validity. Further, their exception
did not cover damage to other work caused by any defective Gillig Corporation part types. Staff deemed
these exceptions to be unacceptable and considered their offer non-compliant and not considered further.

Each contract includes approximately 10% contingency for variances between forecasted and actual usage
and new parts yet to be identified which may be added to the contracts during the contract term.

The pricing for the new one-year inventory supply contracts are approximately 22% higher in the year of the
recommended contract. Staff investigated the causes of this increase and noted that the current existing
contract with Midwest Bus Corporation contained pricing that was approximately 26% lower than the pre-
contract pricing. Subsequent to issuing the existing contract, Midwest Bus Corporation contacted staff and
advised that they had made an error in their quoted prices by not indicating that they were quoting in US
dollars. Their claim was reviewed and denied by staff and Midwest Bus Corporation honoured their prices.
During the claim review, staff did note that the next lowest price was approximately 23% higher than that of
the current Midwest Bus Corporation contract. On this basis, staff considers this price increase to be
acceptable.

Though pricing was received in years 2 and 3, staff have considered it too high to recommend acceptance at
this time and maintain acceptance of the one-year contract term.


JUSTIFICATION

These Lift-U parts are required in order to maintain the wheelchair lifts on the Commission’s equipped
buses.

SUBJECT: Procurement Authorization – Asphalt Repairs And Maintenance

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Commission authorize the acceptance of the tender submitted
by IPAC Paving Ltd., in the upset limit of $380,000.00, for the repair and maintenance of
on-grade pavement at various Commission properties for the contract period May 1, 2003
to April 30, 2005.



FUNDING

Sufficient funds for 2003 expenditures are included in the 2003 TTC Operating Budget.
Sufficient funds will also be included in the 2004 and 2005 TTC Operating Budgets as
required.



BACKGROUND

The Commission has a large number of on-grade paved areas including subway station
and rapid transit station bus roadways, loops, yards, garages, carhouses and other facility
pavements. Some of these pavements are well over 25 years old, thus exceeding their
accepted economical life.

When subjected to roadway salt, heavy loading from buses and freeze-thaw cycles, these
paved areas often develop extensive cracking and heaving and create tripping and
liability hazards for both patrons and employees. Ongoing rehabilitative repairs and
maintenance programs are required to ensure safe use for both pedestrians and traffic.



DISCUSSION

Specifications were prepared for the repair and maintenance of asphalt pavement at
various Commission properties. Thirteen companies were invited to submit tenders, in
addition to the public advertisement on the Commission’s Web Site on February 13,
2003, out of which eight companies submitted tenders, as detailed on the attached
Appendix "A".

IPAC Paving Ltd. submitted the lowest tendered amount based on the estimated two-year
quantities. IPAC Paving Ltd. did not take any exceptions/qualifications and are
recommended for an upset limit amount award of $380,000.00, which includes a
 contingency of approximately 10% for variation in usage over the two years of the
contract.

IPAC Paving Ltd. is the current supplier and their pricing is approximately 13.1% lower
than currently paid to the same vendor from a January, 2001 tender. IPAC Paving’s
second year pricing is the same as their Year 1 pricing.

All of the remaining submissions did not take any exceptions/qualifications, but were not
considered further due to their higher pricing.



JUSTIFICATION

Continuation of the service for the repair and maintenance of on-grade asphalt pavement
is necessary in order to maintain the safety of all Commission properties.

SUBJECT: Purchase Of Ford Parts




RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Commission authorize the following for inventory:

1. Additional funds for the purchase order with Thorncrest Sherway Incorporated for $158,000 resulting in
a revised upset limit of $1,108,000.

2. The award of an inventory supply contract for the supply of various Ford parts to Donway Ford Sales
Limited for $286,000, including applicable taxes, for the period following Commission approval to April
2008:


FUNDING

Sufficient funds to cover these items have been included in the 2006 TTC Operating Budget and will be
included in future budgets as required. These inventory materials will be charged to the appropriate budget
at the time of issuance from Stores.


BACKGROUND

Over the past few years, staff has undertaken measures to use multiple year inventory supply contracts.
These contracts allow the Commission the opportunity for improved pricing and committed vendor lead-
time. During the course of these contracts, new parts are identified which necessitates the need to have
them added to existing contracts. To accomplish this, staff issues proposals and subsequently recommend
awarding accordingly.

The subject Ford parts are used for varying ELF Wheel-Trans bus maintenance needs. Several examples
include wiper motors, driver seat bases and engine modules.

At its meeting of May 11, 2005, the Commission approved the award of three-year inventory supply
contracts for various Ford parts for the period from May 2005 to April 2008 for 297 part types to:
 •               Thorncrest Sherway Incorporated for $950,000 including applicable taxes.

•               Yorkdale Ford Lincoln Sales for $82,000 including applicable taxes.

Subsequent to those awards, 70 additional part types were identified as candidates to be added to the
existing contracts.


DISCUSSION

Proposals were invited from nine known companies coupled with an advertisement on the TTC internet
website on March 16, 2006. Two companies submitted proposals as summarized in Appendix ‘A’. The
remaining seven companies did not submit proposals because they felt they would not be competitive, could
not provide firm pricing or did not have enough time to respond.

The proposal called for 70 pre-approved part types. The proponents were also advised that alternatives
would not be considered during the evaluation. A total of 69 part types are being recommended for award.
The 1 part type that is not being recommended for award was removed during the evaluation as it was
determined that that part type is obsolete.

Thorncrest Sherway Incorporated submitted prices on 69 part types and has the lowest compliant price on 2
part types. They are recommended to be awarded these 2 part types totalling $158,000 resulting in a revised
upset limit contract for $1,108,000.

Donway Ford Sales Limited submitted prices on 69 part types and has the lowest compliant price on 67 part
types. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $286,000 for 67 part types.

Each contract includes approximately 15% contingency for variances between forecasted and actual usage
and new parts yet to be identified which may be added to the contracts during the contract term.

The pricing for the amended and new inventory supply contracts are approximately 1% lower in the first
year of the contract. The pricing will be approximately 2% higher in year two based on year one pricing.


JUSTIFICATION

These various Ford parts are required in order to support varying Wheel-Trans bus maintenance needs.

                SUBJECT: Purchase Of Switch Lock Box Parts




                RECOMMENDATION

                It is recommended that the Commission authorize the award of a five-year inventory supply contract for the
                supply of various switch lock box parts to Niagara Track and Castings Incorporated for the period from
                April 2006 to April 2011 for an upset limit of $695,000 including applicable taxes.


                FUNDING

                Sufficient funds to cover these items have been included in the 2006 TTC Operating Budget and will be
                included in future budgets as required. These inventory materials will be charged to the appropriate budget
                at the time of issuance from Stores.


                BACKGROUND

                The subject switch lock box parts are used to maintain the surface track streetcar switches. These switch
                lock box parts are used in the maintenance of streetcar switches.

                One of the parts is the complete switch lock box assembly and the other 13 part types are the individual
                components that go into the complete switch lock box assembly. In the past awards for this requirement
                were based on the lowest compliant bid for each part and several vendors were awarded different parts.
                However, in order to get the different parts manufactured by different companies to fit together in the switch
                lock box assembly, machine shop work was required before the parts could be used by the Commission
                resulting in additional cost and delay. The existing tooling/patterns for these parts are at the end of their
                useful life and the proponents were requested to price the cost for the new tooling/patterns for these parts
                (the tooling/patterns will be the property of the TTC).             To correct past problems with the
 interchangeability/fit within each switch lock box assembly, the award of contract was based on the lowest
overall bid for all the parts in the proposal.


DISCUSSION

Proposals were invited from thirteen known companies coupled with an advertisement on the TTC internet
website on December 23, 2005. Four companies submitted proposals as summarized in Appendix ‘A’.
The proposal called for 14 pre-approved part types. Further, the proponents were requested to include
tooling costs as well as being advised that alternatives would not be considered during the evaluation. Their
proposals were required also to include a Quality Plan and ISO certification. A total of 14 part types are
being recommended for award.

Niagara Track and Castings Incorporated submitted prices on all 14 part types and has the lowest compliant
price on 14 part types. Their proposal did not state any exceptions or qualifications and is considered
commercially complaint. They are recommended to be awarded an upset limit contract for $695,000 for the
14 part types.

H.J. Skelton Canada Ltd. submitted prices on 14 part types and did not have the lowest overall submitted
prices. They submitted all the mandatory submission requirements. Their submission did not state any
exceptions or qualifications.

Ronsco Incorporated submitted prices on 14 part types and has the second lowest price on 14 part types.
However, they did not submit the required Quality Plan or any ISO certification and, therefore, they are
considered commercially non-compliant.

D.J. Industrial Sales submitted prices on 14 part types and had the highest price on all items. However, they
did not submit their Quality Plan as required and, therefore, they are considered commercially non-
compliant.

The recommended upset limit includes approximately 20% contingency for variances between forecasted
and actual usage and new parts yet to be identified which may be added to the contract during the contract
period.

The pricing for the new five-year inventory supply contracts are approximately 11% higher in the first year
of the contract. The pricing will be approximately 2% higher in year two based on year one pricing;
approximately 6% higher in year three based on year two pricing; approximately 6% higher in year four
based on year three pricing and approximately 5% higher in year five based on year four pricing. The price
increase is attributed to charges in the material specifications for some of the parts as well as tighter
tolerances required for the new parts to ensure a more consistent fit of the parts in the assembly and a more
expensive method of manufacturing most of the components is required, i.e. investment casting process.


JUSTIFICATION

These switch lock box parts are required in order to support streetcar surface track maintenance needs.

A number of existing station facilities on the Bloor-Danforth Subway have not had any

facilities are now over 40 years old and are showing signs of wear and age. The Station
Modernization Program aims to upgrade and modernize both indoor and outdoor public
spaces on the Bloor-Danforth Subway to provide station facilities that are:

-   In a state of good repair, maintainable and safe;
-   More easily navigated with excellent wayfinding assists at all levels;
-   Visually modern and more identifiable as a TTC transit facility; and,

Commission on June 13, 2007 and the station finishes and artwork were approved on May

Material Payment Bond each in the amount of 50% of the total contract value.

SUBJECT: Notice Of Award Of Procurement Authorization Jane Station Structural
Paving Rehabilitation Contract W2-2



RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Commission receive the notice of award of Chair Disero,
Commissioner Ashton and the Chief General Manager to authorize acceptance of the
tender submitted by Anscon Contracting Inc. in the amount of $456,000.00, for Contract
W2-2 – Jane Station – Structural Paving Rehabilitation.



FUNDING

Sufficient funds for this expenditure are included in project 3.4 Bridges and Structures,
under Structural Paving Rehabilitation Program, as set out on pages 551 to 558 of the
State of Good Repair/Safety Category) of the TTC 2002-2006 Capital Program, which
was approved by City Council on March 6, 2002.



BACKGROUND

At its meeting of October 20, 1999, the Commission approved the revisions and updates
to the Authorization for Expenditures Policy/Instruction, which states that "The
Commission delegates authority to the Chair, Vice-Chair and Chief General Manager to
authorize items on an interim basis that would normally be authorized by the
Commission when the approval is required before the next Commission meeting. The
interim authorization is to be followed up by a notice of award Commission report that is
to be submitted to the next scheduled meeting."

The Jane Station, which was constructed in 1964, is located just north of Bloor on Jane
Street along the Bloor Danforth Subway line. The station includes a Bus Transfer Facility
for TTC patrons to interchange with the subway system below grade.

After nearly 40 years of service certain structural elements have deteriorated and are in
need of remedial work. A detailed condition survey completed in 2001 recommended that
the proposed rehabilitation measures be undertaken at this time.

DISCUSSION
 In general, the work includes removal of the existing asphalt and waterproofing over the
mezzanine roof slab, localized removal and repair of deteriorated concrete and the
installation of concrete overlay with a waterproofing membrane.

Tender documents were prepared for Contract W2-2, Jane Station – Structural Paving
Rehabilitation and a Request for Tenders was posted on TTC’s web site as of July 24,
2002. Nine companies requested copies of tender documents out of which seven
submitted tenders as summarized in Appendix ‘A’.

The lowest tender was received from Anscon Contracting Inc. in the amount of
$456,000.00 and included no exceptions or qualifications to the tender documents. As
they have not previously worked for the Commission in the past, reference checks were
completed which indicate that they have satisfactorily performed work of a similar size
and nature. They are considered commercially and technically acceptable.

Based on a review of the contractor’s financial statements, it appears they have the
financial capability to perform this contract.

Torbridge Construction Ltd. submitted the second lowest priced tender and also did not
state any exceptions or qualifications and are considered commercially and technically
compliant.



JUSTIFICATION

The tender submitted by Anscon Contracting Inc. is the lowest priced compliant tender.

Recommendation
